profiles.summary: The official endpoint still answers nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f on linux-arm64 with go1.27.3, and the v3.13.0 source is still not published. New this cycle: the Pocket gateway rotates between v3.12.4+960ca0a and the PublicNode-style vlocal+5f02f3f-modified build from one request to the next, and the Nitro source shows that the -modified suffix is Go's vcs.modified flag, which any uncommitted or untracked file in the build tree sets.

deltas.delta: arb-one.api.pocket.network answered nitro/vlocal+5f02f3f-20261014T220458Z-modified at the start of the L-1089 run (about 17:15Z) and nitro/v3.12.4+960ca0a at 17:09Z and six times at 17:21Z on 2026-11-26, so one URL is served by two builds.

The -modified suffix comes from vcs.modified in the Go build settings when the linker stamp is empty (nitroversion/current.go lines 55-90 and version.go lines 158-170 at 5f02f3f); Go sets it when git status --porcelain prints anything (cmd/go/internal/vcs/vcs.go lines 233-237 at go1.25.12). It says nothing about which files changed.
arbitrum-one-rpc.publicnode.com and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com answered the third web3_clientVersion within one second with a Cloudflare managed challenge page.
go.mod of OffchainLabs/nitro still returns 404 at v3.13.0, v3.13.0-rc.9, rc.10, rc.11, v3.13.1, v3.13.2 and b72783f, and 200 at v3.12.4 and master.

The official endpoint routes each request and each batch element independently between the amd64 and arm64 backends; in this cycle's brackets the two appeared in a ratio close to one to one.

profiles.summary: Elysium still answers nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown on go1.25.12. Read against the Nitro version code, that string means the binary carries neither a linker stamp nor Go VCS build settings, so it was built from a tree without git metadata. The node answers eth_config with the same 36 precompiles as the rc.9 build, ArbFilteredTransactionsManager at 0x74 included, and it does not serve arb_getRawBlockMetadata, which both Arbitrum One builds asked serve. These answers narrow the build but do not name it.

eth_config on Elysium returns the same 36 precompiles as Arbitrum One, forkId 0x8ac7c738, and arb_getRawBlockMetadata answers method not found.

cleared.check: Lead L-1109: does Nitro rc.9 b72783f give the specified word on the targeted set, the battery and script set 1 when the answer comes from the linux-amd64 backend of Robinhood Chain, which had no targeted or pmdiff run.
cleared.result: Robinhood Chain's endpoint routes every request, and every element of a batch, to an amd64 or an arm64 backend on its own (three-element web3_clientVersion batches came back mixed, raw/clientversion.txt), so a bracket cannot pin one eth_call. Each batch was therefore sent several times, each send bracketed. targeted.py: 143 batches of 600 vectors sent 8 times each (1,144 eth_calls), 0 mismatches; every batch had at least two sends with an amd64 bracket and 127 had a send with amd64 on both sides. battery.py: 167 batches sent 6 times (1,002 eth_calls), 0 mismatches, 167 of 167 with an amd64 bracket. pmdiff.py with this checkout's build (code sha256 equal to cycle 25's a7aaa3ba): 250 scripts sent 8 times (2,000 eth_calls), every answer identical to the cycle 25 Ethereum reference hash, 226 scripts with an amd64-amd64 bracketed send. The brackets read amd64 4,155 times and arm64 4,135 times, so with independent routing near one half the chance that a given targeted batch never reached amd64 in 8 sends is 1/256 and for a pmdiff script in 8 sends 1/256. No arithmetic, jump, memory or PoolManager result differs between the two architectures, so the lines of FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, TickMath and BitMath that these vectors and scripts drive compute the same on both.

cleared.result: 371,058 vectors answered, 0 mismatches. Both builds carry the ArbOS 61 upgrade (v3.11.2 arbos/arbosState/arbosstate.go line 504) and report arbOSVersion 116. Blockvectra refused some bracket calls with HTTP 429; no eth_call was refused. These endpoints only answer reads; they do not produce Robinhood Chain blocks.

cleared.check: Lead L-1089: replay of the three swaps of Arbitrum One transaction 0x06c45e8173f93894c692e60faa0143c301774a28cfca70de399b1d6520fe06f0 (block 527,671,975) from the state the chain actually ran it on.
cleared.result: Pocket served debug_traceTransaction with prestateTracer. The prestate holds 15 PoolManager words; pool 0x4dff5a7f starts at sqrtPriceX96 0xa51c97dc2497e2b3c9724807, tick -8772 and liquidity 0x17bebb6dde73e7, which is exactly the end state of the Swap at log index 0x4 of transaction 0xa9ffc511 earlier in the block (its parent-block slot0 is tick 65,494). Its Slot0 word gives an LP fee of 770,000 and protocol fees of 1,000 each way, so a swap fee of 770,230 as in the event. The bitmap has bits only at compressed ticks -115 and 115, which bounds the tick spacing to 7,656 to 7,715, outside the candidate list of tools/opdiff/replay.py; that, together with the parent-block start, is why cycle 25 and the in-block replay with the old list did not reproduce it. With the spacing added, all three swaps (log indices 15, 16, 17) reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit as exact-input swaps with an open limit, reading only words present in the prestate on the successful path.

cleared.check: Does any of the three nodes route an address to native precompile code that the earlier precompile sweeps (0x01 to 0x1ff, 0x64 to 0x74, 0xc8, 0xff, 0xa4b05) did not call from the PoolManager address.
cleared.result: No. eth_config (the node's own report of its active configuration) returns the same 36 addresses on all three chains: 0x01 to 0x11, 0x64 to 0x69, 0x6b to 0x74, 0xff, 0x100 and 0xa4b05, all inside the swept ranges, plus the EIP-2935 history contract, which an earlier sweep also called and which reverts on every PoolManager call shape.

cleared.check: Holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and the Nitro go-ethereum handlers as interpreter state that outlives one instruction (the cycle 25 critic's point about long sequences with alternating inputs).
cleared.result: Neither keeps state between instructions on the arithmetic path. uint256.go at v1.3.2 has one package-level table (pows, line 1352 onward, constant) and no cache, and MulMod computes the reciprocal of a four-limb modulus afresh on every call (uint256.go lines 720-729, Reciprocal and reduce4 in mod.go) and otherwise divides with udivrem. opDiv, opSdiv, opMod, opSmod, opExp, opSignExtend, opByte, opAddmod, opMulmod, opSHL, opSHR and opSAR in the OffchainLabs go-ethereum fork call the library on stack values only (core/vm/instructions.go lines 51-235 of the copy read in cycle 25), and opKeccak256 resets the hasher on every call (lines 236-249). The only per-code cache, jump destination analysis keyed by code, was tested in cycle 15. The pmdiff scripts, which run thousands of mixed mulDiv, shift and division sequences in one call, match on both architectures above.

cleared.check: ArbOS state that changes what the PoolManager's native and token paths meet: scheduled upgrade, native token management, transaction filtering, calldata price flag, chain owners and ArbOS version, read at the head on 2026-11-26.

leads.question: Which Nitro build produces Robinhood Chain blocks? The official endpoint answers rc.9 b72783f, and public endpoints answer v3.12.0, v3.11.2 and a modified v3.12.2 snapshot.
leads.why: Every opcode result in this review describes the node that answered, and only the sequencer's build writes pool state. No public statement names it.

Each batch was therefore sent several times, each send bracketed. targeted.py: 143 batches of 600 vectors sent 8 times each (1,144 eth_calls), 0 mismatches; every batch had at least two sends with an amd64 bracket and 127 had a send with amd64 on both sides. battery.py: 167 batches sent 6 times (1,002 eth_calls), 0 mismatches, 167 of 167 with an amd64 bracket. pmdiff.py with this checkout's build (code sha256 equal to cycle 25's a7aaa3ba): 250 scripts sent 8 times (2,000 eth_calls), every answer identical to the cycle 25 Ethereum reference hash, 226 scripts with an amd64-amd64 bracketed send. Closed. Pocket now serves the prestate trace of the transaction. The pool starts at the end state of the earlier swap of transaction 0xa9ffc511 in the same block, and its tick spacing is between 7,656 and 7,715 (bitmap bits at compressed ticks -115 and 115), which the replay's candidate list lacked. With that spacing all three swaps of the transaction reproduce to the unit from the prestate (raw/l1089-prestate-replay.json).

The changes cannot be read. The -modified suffix is Go's vcs.modified flag, set when git status --porcelain prints anything in the build tree, including an untracked file (nitroversion/current.go and version.go at 5f02f3f; cmd/go/internal/vcs/vcs.go lines 233-237 at go1.25.12), so it does not show that code under core/vm, state or precompiles changed. The same build string now also answers on robinhood-rpc.publicnode.com and, from time to time, behind arb-one.api.pocket.network. arbitrum-one-rpc.publicnode.com answered with a Cloudflare challenge after two requests, so no new vectors were run against it this cycle; cycle 25 recorded 230,061 matching vectors on it.

Partly answered. b9abbcc resolves in paradigmxyz/reth on raw.githubusercontent.com and its Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and version.rs are byte identical to the v2.11.0 tag and differ from main, which fits the tag commit; the full id of the tag could not be read (GitHub API, release page and codeload answer 403). The PublicNode Arbitrum One build stays as in L-1090. The Polygon part belongs to another unit.

Not attempted for Robinhood Chain. The cycle was set on the interpreter, and the census rule balances transfers against Swap events, so it cannot see an amount the PoolManager computed wrongly; the gap 6,057,070 to 117,163,726 stays as listed. The other networks of the lead belong to other units.

Elysium half only. debug_traceBlockByNumber, trace_block and debug_traceCall still answer authenticated API key required, chainid.network lists rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz as the only public endpoint, and the explorer's /explorer/api/v2 and /api/v2 paths now return a Vercel security checkpoint page, which was not worked around. Frames without value cannot be listed, so the question still needs a keyed trace provider.
